description: Around 72,000 people of Nigerian origin lived in Germany as of November 2019, the largest sub-Saharan African community in the country. BAMF expanded the number of offices handling Nigerian asylum claims because Nigeria became one of the ten largest countries of origin worldwide.
energy_note: Large enough community to need its own processing capacity.

aspect: The formal-decision share, and what observers conclude from it
description: Reporting notes the proportion of purely formal decisions on Nigerian applications is very high compared with other countries of origin, with the conclusion drawn that Black refugees are not especially welcome. A formal decision is one that never reaches the question of whether the person is in danger.
energy_note: Decided without anyone asking what happened to you.

description: BAMF frequently declares claims inadmissible under Dublin and orders removal to Italy. If the transfer is not effected within six months, Germany becomes responsible again and the procedure begins afresh - so the applicant waits, is told to leave, is not moved, and starts over.
energy_note: Six months of being about to be deported, then back to the start.

aspect: Most deportations of Nigerians are not to Nigeria
description: Many people with Nigerian nationality are deported each year, but predominantly to Italy rather than to Nigeria. The removal is intra-European and the person's actual country never enters the transaction.
energy_note: Deported, and not to the country you are from.

aspect: Missing travel documents suspend removals, which helps nobody
description: The commonest reason deportations are suspended is a lack of travel documents, with the Nigerian embassy slow to issue them. The result is not safety but limbo: not removable, not regularised, not permitted to work.
energy_note: Unremovable and unsettled, at the same time.

aspect: EXAMPLE - refused for being able to hide
description: A Nigerian man in his early thirties claimed asylum in Germany on grounds of persecution for his homosexuality. BAMF argued it was disputed how strongly the relevant legislation is enforced, and refused; he litigated. Rejecting queer claimants on the basis that they could conceal themselves at home has been repeatedly criticised as unlawful.
energy_note: Refused because the law against you is only sometimes enforced.
